articles.headline: Sources: Jets RB Breece Hall week-to-week with quad injury
articles.description: Jets running back Breece Hall, who suffered a quad injury in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, is considered week-to-week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets running back Breece Hall, who injured his right quadriceps Sunday, is considered week-to-week, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Monday.

There was some sense of relief, as an MRI showed that Hall avoided a long-term injury, a source said. Nevertheless, he likely won't be ready to play Sunday against the Chicago Bears, a blow to the Jets' already struggling rushing attack.

After a 152-yard rushing day in the opener, the Jets (1-2) managed only 67 and 58 yards in Weeks 2 and 3, including only 61 yards on 29 carries (2.1-yard average) for Hall. The Jets will lean heavily on third-year backs Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis while Hall is sidelined.

Injuries are mounting for the Jets, who played without wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions. Their status for Sunday is uncertain.

Coach Aaron Glenn provided no update Monday on Hall or left guard Dylan Parham (knee), who also was injured Sunday.

"[The run game] is one area that we have to fix," said Glenn, adding there's an "urgency in trying to make sure that we get that done, because that's been a strong point of ours, especially after the first game. To have these two games to where we didn't run it as well, that's something that we have to dial into to make sure that we get those things fixed."

The Jets identified Hall as a foundational piece on offense, signing him to a three-year, $43.5 million extension in the offseason. He missed three weeks in training camp due to a strained groin but came out hot in the opener with a 102-yard, one-touchdown game in the 23-10 win over the Tennessee Titans.

On his 13th and final carry in Detroit, Hall was tackled out of bounds early in the fourth quarter and rolled over in pain, clutching his right thigh.

After the game, Hall said he "felt something when I was running and then got tackled and planted and then felt something else."

The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Sept. 28

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons 'didn't touch a ball for a year'

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer ahead of big decision

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren would hold veto power on any trade this season and is an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent, is key.

There are eight projected teams who have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at Media Day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during the Pistons' Media Day. -- Bobby Marks

At Cavaliers Media Day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

articles.headline: Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past Leonard investigation
articles.description: The LA Clippers opened media day on Monday by apologizing to fans in the wake of an NBA salary cap circumvention investigation that levied stiff penalties on the organization.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The LA Clippers opened media day on Monday by apologizing to fans in the wake of an NBA salary cap circumvention investigation that levied stiff penalties on the organization.

With owner Steve Ballmer, president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank and president of business operations Gillian Zucker all serving league-mandated suspensions, interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden said the organization was committed to regaining the trust of their fan base.

"Our fans deserve to hear from us before this, and for that we're sorry," Redden said. "We've been listening to the thoughts, the concerns, and feeling the emotions of our fan base. They mean everything to us. Their pain through this time is real, and we feel it and we hear them, as well as our staff members who are proud to be part of this organization. We hope to fulfill our promises to them to build their trust and move forward."

The Clippers announced last week that John S. Gibson, a Los Angeles area lawyer, would serve as the organization's interim governor during Ballmer's year-long suspension. Gibson said in an online video that the Clippers were committed to three goals: "building bridges" across the basketball community, improving the "culture of compliance" with league rules, and executing a "comprehensive review" of the organization's basketball and business operations.

Meanwhile, Redden has stepped in for Frank during his six-month suspension. Redden, who joined the Clippers in 2017, will be supported by longtime coach Ty Lue and a front office staff that includes interim general manager Mark Hughes and executive Lee Jenkins.

"Our processes of how we go through talking to teams and drumming up ideas and figuring out what might work for us, both short and long term, stays the same," Redden said. "Ty's input on the player level and his system is always part of it. I don't see that changing because of the [suspensions]. We'll just talk to [Gibson] for final approval [of trades] instead of talking to [Ballmer]."

The NBA's investigation concluded that the Clippers broke league rules by arranging endorsement opportunities for All-Star forward Kawhi Leonard, who was traded to the Toronto Raptors earlier this month. In addition to the suspensions, the Clippers were forced to pay a $30 million fine and forfeit five first-round picks. The Clippers initially "rejected the NBA's findings" when the investigation's results were released in August, but Ballmer eventually changed course and said he would accept the league's punishments in a Sept. 13 statement.

"The penalties we are facing are significant, and we will comply with them," Redden said.

Lue said he remains committed to the Clippers and is "loyal to the end" to Ballmer, who hired him as head coach in 2020. Lue praised his players for working out together in Los Angeles in recent weeks, noting that the "morale is great, even in these tough situations."

articles.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. to sit with hamstring injury
articles.description: Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. will miss time with a hamstring injury suffered in Sunday's loss to the Raiders. New Orleans coach Kellen Moore did not specify how long Etienne will be out.
articles.body:
METAIRIE, La. -- New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore said running back Travis Etienne Jr. will miss time with a hamstring issue.

Moore did not specify how long Etienne will be out or if he will have to go on injured reserve. Etienne went to the locker room midway through the third quarter of the Saints' 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders and did not return.

Etienne began grabbing at his left hamstring shortly before going out of bounds following a 16-yard run in the third quarter. He was pushed out of bounds by a defensive player and grabbed at his leg again while on the ground. Etienne got up on his own and limped to the opposite sideline, then went into the injury tent before going to the locker room.

Etienne had been on the injury report leading up to the game with a hamstring issue but participated fully in Friday's practice. Moore said the injury occurred on the same leg as the one that had been bothering him during the week.

Etienne had a season-high 19 carries for 57 yards before the injury. After he left, carries were split between Alvin Kamara (six carries after Etienne's injury) and Kendre Miller (four carries after Etienne's injury). Kamara, who missed time with a knee injury in September, had nine carries in his season debut against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2 over Etienne's eight carries, although the Saints almost exclusively used Etienne as the main rusher in the first half of the Raiders game.

Kamara, Miller and rookie CJ Donaldson will likely all be used in the Saints' Week 4 game against the Atlanta Falcons next Monday night. Kamara is second on the team with 18 carries for 51 yards despite missing the season opener, while Miller, who was a healthy inactive against the Ravens, is third with 13 carries for 44 yards and a touchdown.

articles.headline: Owner Mat Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt Suns
articles.description: Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia says financial issues at his mortgage company will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball.
articles.body:
PHOENIX -- It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

"How does it affect the Phoenix Suns when (the mortgage company has) a bad month, or a bad quarter, or a bad year, or a bad three years?" Ishbia said. "It affects zero. Absolutely zero. It's got nothing to do with anything."

Ishbia added that UWM still employs 9,000 people and is in a fine position going forward. He bought the Suns and the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury in 2022 for $4 billion and has quickly developed a reputation for spending money.

"We had a bad quarter," Ishbia said of UWM. "People like to create stories out of thin air and create a bunch of negativity. When we have a great quarter this quarter I don't think I'll see all the articles. But anyway, it's part of my life and part of what it is. The mortgage company's doing great -- not that anyone really cares."

The Suns are coming off a 45-37 season and return most of the team, including star guard Devin Booker, forward Dillon Brooks and guard Jalen Green.

articles.headline: Sources: Vikings' Jefferson has ankle sprain, could play this week
articles.description: Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson has an ankle sprain, according to the MRI performed Monday, and there's a chance he is able to play Sunday against the Dolphins, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Dan Graziano.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson has an ankle sprain, according to the MRI performed Monday, and there's a chance he is able to play Sunday against the Miami Dolphins, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Dan Graziano.

Jefferson did not return Sunday after suffering a left ankle injury at the end of the Vikings' first possession in a 23-16 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers that improved Minnesota to 3-0 this season.

Coach Kevin O'Connell said after Sunday's game that Jefferson was "pretty close" to returning to the game but "just couldn't get there."

His injury Sunday came at the end of a 10-yard screen pass with 11:07 remaining in the first quarter. He had earlier caught a 22-yard pass across the middle amid high hopes that he and Murray would team up to elevate the passing game.

In his absence, receiver Jordan Addison caught five passes for 90 yards, including a 41-yard touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter. But it was the only offensive touchdown the Vikings scored Sunday as they managed just seven first downs after Jefferson's injury.

At one point after Jefferson's injury, Murray completed only two of 15 passes. He finished the day with 15 completions in 29 attempts for 168 yards, taking three sacks and having a batted pass intercepted in the backfield.

Jefferson, a two-time first-team All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowl selection, has largely been healthy in his NFL career and has played in every Vikings game for five of his six full seasons. The lone exception was a torn right hamstring in 2023 that caused him to miss seven games.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Jokic leaves no doubt on future: 'I'm gonna sign next year'
articles.description: Nikola Jokic left little doubt that he plans to be back in Denver at least next season after saying he plans to sign his extension when its offered next summer.
articles.body:
Nikola Jokic left no doubt on media day about his future with the Denver Nuggets as he enters the final guaranteed year of his contract.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said Monday.

"If they want me," he added.

There's little doubt from Denver's side that they would. The three-time MVP has a player option for next season and was eligible to negotiate a four-year, $278 million extension this offseason. By waiting to sign, Jokic can ink a five-year, $359.5 million contract next summer.

Jokic said he's talked with the leadership team in Denver, including executive V.P. of basketball operations Ben Tenzer, executive V.P. of player personnel John Wallace and Josh Kroenke.

"They know my opinion and I was being more than open about it, and hopefully they trust me," Jokic said.

The Nuggets are coming off a disappointing postseason finish, losing to the Minnesota Timberwolves in the first round last season. Denver has yet to make it past the second round since winning the franchise's first championship in 2023.

The end of the roster has been reshuffled, with restricted free agent Peyton Watson getting moved in a deal to Cleveland. To supplement the bench, the Nuggets re-signed Spencer Jones and added guard Tyus Jones and center Marvin Bagley III.

articles.headline: Clippers' Brandon Ingram to miss start of season after surgery
articles.description: Brandon Ingram, a key part of the Clippers' return in their trade of Kawhi Leonard, will not be available to start the 2026-27 season as he recovers from a surgery that addressed a right heel injury and partially torn Achilles tendon.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Clippers forward Brandon Ingram will not be available to start the 2026-27 season as he recovers from a surgery that addressed a right heel injury and partially torn Achilles tendon.

Interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden said at Clippers media day Monday that doctors discovered and addressed the previously undisclosed Achilles injury while Ingram underwent surgery on his heel in May.

Ingram, 29, has no timetable for a return to the court, but Redden noted that the recovery time for a partially torn Achilles tendon is typically "about six months less" than for a fully torn Achilles. Ingram missed the final two games of the Raptors' first-round series loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers due to the heel injury before undergoing surgery.

The Clippers acquired Ingram and guard Gradey Dick from the Toronto Raptors in a trade for Kawhi Leonard earlier this month.

"It wasn't until we got our hands on [Ingram] here that we started to see where he was at with his progression," Redden said. "He won't be ready for the start of the season, and we'll reevaluate when we get there."

Ingram characterized his rehabilitation timeline as a "week-by-week thing" and said he won't "be participating in training camp much, but I'll be out there a little bit."

"I'm doing well in my recovery," he said. "I'm coming along. I've been in the facility for a little more than a month now. Getting on the court a little bit and getting stronger.

"I had been dealing with some pain throughout the year with the Raptors and especially coming down in crunch time. I didn't quite know what it was. Near the end of the season, we figured out what it was. We thought surgery was the best thing to do."

Redden also said guard Bradley Beal is dealing with right knee inflammation after undergoing surgery on his left hip and won't be available for the start of training camp.

Ingram, a two-time All-Star, averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists for the Raptors last season. Once he returns to the court, Ingram projects as the leading scoring option for the new-look Clippers.

"Whenever [Ingram] comes back, when he gets out there, I think our pick-and-roll will be the No. 1 thing we go to," Clippers guard Darius Garland said. "I think that can be really nasty.

"He's super crafty. I'm super excited to play with him for sure."

Ingram is on the Clippers' books for $40 million this season and holds a $41.9 million player option for 2027-28.

articles.headline: Jaguars sorting out ball boy spat after Travis Hunter interception
articles.description: Jaguars coach Liam Coen isn't sure if cornerback Travis Hunter ended up with the actual ball from his first NFL interception.
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen isn't sure if cornerback Travis Hunter ended up with the actual ball from his first NFL interception.

Hunter spun the ball in celebration and danced after picking off a pass from New England's Drake Maye in the end zone late in the second quarter Sunday.

An NFL ball boy picked it up and then refused to give it to Josh Hines-Allen, even screaming, "Hey, you can't touch me!" when the Jaguars pass rusher tried to grab the ball.

NFL players are allowed to keep game balls, although they get charged a hefty price by the league.

Hines-Allen tried to knock this one out of the ball boy's hands before Jacksonville's equipment manager, George Pellicer, stepped between them.

The ball boy again screamed, "Hey, he pushed me. He can't do that!" as Pellicer worked to retrieve the ball.

Video of the interaction went viral hours after the game, which the Jaguars won 35-6.

"I was just talking about it," Coen said during a Zoom call with reporters Monday. "I haven't gotten a clean answer. We've been in communication with those guys over there. I think they've gotten it sorted out; I can't say for certain if we got the actual ball or not.

"I know there was something that went on there. I think it's all squared away. We'll get it taken care of."

Hunter, the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner and second overall draft pick, out of Colorado, made a leaping catch on the pass intended for Patriots receiver Efton Chism III. The play prevented New England from cutting into a 14-3 lead just before the break.

"The coach did a great job scheming it up for us," Hunter said after the game. "He called the perfect call for us. We all talked and we communicated on my side of the ball, and I just made it happen."
